```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#", fig.width = 5,
                      fig.height = 3, fig.align = "center", dpi = 120)
```

`susie_get_cs_attainable()` screens fitted effects when genotype data
and reference LD are unavailable for purity filtering. For each effect,
*attainable coverage* is the sum of its original inclusion probabilities
over variants for which it has the highest inclusion probability among
effects. Ties count for each tied effect. An effect passes if its
attainable coverage exceeds `coverage` and its entropy over these
variants is below `log(ethres)`. To construct each reported set, susieR
ranks variants using the full single-effect posterior and adds them until
their original probabilities sum to at least `coverage`.

We use the attainable coverage criterion introduced by
[SparsePro (Zhang et al. 2023)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1011104)
to screen effects. The paper describes reporting sets at the requested
coverage for effects that pass. At 95%, the
[released code](https://github.com/zhwm/SparsePro/blob/e13ac87d6e650d7682ff1f33f6f9898d66932d64/sparsepro_zld.py#L65-L85)
targets $0.95A$, where $A$ is the rounded attainable mass, and can stop
sooner if the next weight is below 0.01. A reported set can therefore
contain less than 95% of the full posterior.

## Example

```{r}
library(susieR)
set.seed(1)
data(N3finemapping)
X <- N3finemapping$X
y <- N3finemapping$Y[, 1]
```

Fit SuSiE with a fixed prior so noise effects are not shrunken away:

```{r}
fitted <- susie(X, y, L = 20,
                estimate_prior_variance = FALSE,
                scaled_prior_variance = 0.05,
                verbose = FALSE)
```

With the genotype matrix available, `susie_get_cs()` filters by
purity:

```{r}
sets_purity <- susie_get_cs(fitted, X = X, coverage = 0.95)
length(sets_purity$cs)
```

Without `X` or `Xcorr`, several poorly localized effects slip through:

```{r}
sets_noLD <- suppressMessages(susie_get_cs(fitted, coverage = 0.95))
length(sets_noLD$cs)
sapply(sets_noLD$cs, length)
```

`susie_get_cs_attainable()` recovers the purity-filtered result
without using `X`:

```{r}
sets_attain <- susie_get_cs_attainable(fitted, coverage = 0.95)
length(sets_attain$cs)
```

The two filters select the same effects:

```{r}
sets_purity$cs
sets_attain$cs
```

## References

Zhang, W., Najafabadi, H., Li, Y. (2023). SparsePro: An efficient
fine-mapping method integrating summary statistics and functional
annotations. *PLOS Genetics* **19**, e1011104.
doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1011104.
